Maladaptive Strategies.value: I dwell on what I have done wrong
I gamble to distract myself or feel excitement
Any situation that might involve disagreement or confrontation

Threat.value: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people
Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
I can't deal with even the slightest upset
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

vignette:
Kwame was twenty-three years old, an ambitious urban planner, dedicated to designing spaces that fostered community and connection. Yet, beneath the surface of his professional aspirations lay a tumultuous world shaped by trauma. The memory of the assault haunted him, a chilling reminder of a night that had irrevocably altered his view of safety and trust. He found himself grappling with a heavy weight of anxiety and confusion, and as he recounted the event in therapy, the details flooded back with vivid intensity.

It had been an ordinary evening, one that spiraled into chaos when a group of men confronted him outside a bar. The argument had erupted suddenly, igniting a fire of aggression that seemed to engulf him. As one of them hurled a beer bottle in his direction, time seemed to slow. Kwame could still see the glint of glass as it shattered against the pavement, the sound a harbinger of the violence that followed. That night had left him with only fragmented images—the flash of angry faces, the crack of glass, and the overwhelming scent of alcohol swirling in the air. Now, he often replayed these snapshots in his mind, each moment locked away as if in a frame, yet he struggled to articulate the pain they invoked. When he attempted to share the details, words eluded him, leaving him overwhelmed and breathless.

In the months that followed, Kwame noticed how his world began to shrink. He became hyper-aware of his surroundings, jumping at the sound of a door slamming or the abrupt laughter of strangers. The very movement of people around him sent jolts of electricity through his body, as if he were still in that moment of danger. Even the calmest expressions of anger made his heart race; he could feel his body tensing as if bracing for impact, convinced that every raised voice could lead to another assault. His friends noticed his withdrawal, but he brushed it off, assuring them he was just busy with work. In reality, he was avoiding any situation that might lead to conflict, convinced that disagreement would spiral out of control, just as it had that night.

To cope, Kwame turned to gambling, seeking excitement in the unpredictable outcomes of games, hoping to drown out the chaos inside his mind with the thrill of chance. Yet, this distraction only deepened his sense of helplessness, each loss serving as a reminder of his inability to control his fate. He often found himself dwelling on what he could have done differently that night, consumed by self-blame and regret. The thought that he could have prevented the attack gnawed at him relentlessly, leading him to conclude that he was somehow responsible for the violence inflicted upon him.

His relationship with safety had been irrevocably altered. Even when others assured him he was safe, he could not shake the feeling that danger lurked just beneath the surface of everyday life. This pervasive sense of distrust extended beyond himself; he felt let down by the very institutions that were supposed to protect him. Reports of crime in his neighborhood seemed to echo his own experience, reinforcing his belief that the world was a fundamentally unsafe place. It became increasingly difficult for him to cope with even minor upsets, as if every small conflict could ignite the same dread he had felt that fateful night.

As Kwame sat in the therapist’s office, he felt a swirl of emotions—fear, hope, and a longing for relief. It was a significant step for him, seeking help after months of isolation and struggle. He had begun to understand that living in this state was unsustainable, yet the fear of confronting his memories made the prospect daunting. What frightened him most was the thought of revisiting that night, of being overwhelmed by the raw emotion that surged when the memories returned. But deep down, he hoped to reclaim his life, to navigate a world free from the shadows of his past. In this moment, he craved the possibility of healing, even as the path ahead appeared steep and fraught with uncertainty.
